formation.title: The Reunification of Kanem-Bornu
formation.text:
The ancient realm of the Sayfawa has been restored. From the shores of Lake Chad to the sands of the Sahara, the lands of Kanem and Bornu are united once more under a single Mai. For centuries the Sayfawa dynasty endured, driven from Kanem by the Bulala, they rebuilt in Bornu, and now they reclaim their heritage.

But what shall define this restored empire? The Mai's armored horsemen are the terror of the Sahel, and the ribats that guard our borders have never been breached. Yet our caravans carry more wealth than our armies seize, natron, cotton, and slaves flow north to Tripoli while horses, salt, and firearms return south. The character of Kanem-Bornu will be decided now, at the moment of its restoration.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: By the lance and the ribat, we are warriors.

modifiers.name: Sword of the Mai
modifiers.text: The Mais of Kanem-Bornu ruled through the strength of their armored cavalry and the fear their iron-helmed warriors inspired across the Sahel. This is an empire forged in battle and held by the lance.

options.text: By the caravan and the market, we are traders.

modifiers.name: Crossroads of the Sahara
modifiers.text: Lake Chad sits at the heart of Africa's greatest trade network. Caravans bearing natron, cotton, and ivory pass through Bornu's markets en route to Tripoli and Fezzan. This is a kingdom made wealthy by commerce, not conquest alone.

advances.name: Kanembu Horsemen
advances.text: The Kanembu cavalry tradition stretches back to the earliest days of the empire, when armored riders dominated the flat grasslands around Lake Chad.

advances.name: Sayfawa Lineage
advances.text: The Sayfawa dynasty claims descent from Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan and has ruled Kanem-Bornu for over seven centuries, the longest-reigning dynasty in recorded history.

advances.name: Natron Extraction
advances.text: The deposits of natron around Lake Chad are among the richest in Africa, providing an essential commodity for trade, preservation, and medicine.

advances.name: Early Islamization
advances.text: The conversion of Kanem to Islam in the 11th century under the Sayfawa reshaped the empire's identity, connecting it to the wider Islamic world.

advances.name: Ribat Tradition
advances.text: Fortified frontier posts guard the empire's borders, serving as both military garrisons and centers of Islamic learning.

advances.name: Lake Chad Fisheries
advances.text: Lake Chad's vast freshwater resources sustain a thriving fishing industry that feeds the empire's growing population.

advances.name: Saharan Caravan Routes
advances.text: Kanem-Bornu sits astride the central trans-Saharan caravan route connecting Lake Chad to Tripoli via Bilma and Fezzan.

advances.name: Ottoman Firearms
advances.text: Turkish military advisors imported by Mai Idris Alooma trained Bornu's soldiers in the use of muskets, creating Africa's first professional gunpowder infantry.

advances.name: Alooma's Reforms
advances.text: Mai Idris Alooma transformed Bornu through military, administrative, and economic reforms, establishing the empire at the height of its power.

event.title: The Reforms of Mai Idris Alooma
event.text:
Mai Idris Alooma has transformed the armies of Bornu. Through diplomatic missions to the Ottoman Porte, he has secured Turkish military advisors who now drill our soldiers in the use of firearms. Iron-helmeted musketeers march alongside the traditional armored cavalry, and fixed military camps with defensive walls have replaced temporary encampments.

Alooma's innovations extend beyond the battlefield. He has cleared the roads for commerce, designed improved boats for Lake Chad's waters, and introduced standard units of measure for grain. His ribat fortifications guard every frontier. The question now is which of his reforms we shall pursue most vigorously.

options.text: The musketeers shall be our vanguard.

modifiers.name: Alooma's Gunpowder Revolution
modifiers.text: Turkish military advisors have trained our musketeers in the arts of firearms warfare, transforming the Bornu army into a modern fighting force.

options.text: The ribats shall secure our borders.

modifiers.name: Alooma's Fortification System
modifiers.text: A network of ribats and fortified camps now secures every frontier of the empire, each garrison a permanent reminder of Bornu's authority.

advances.name: Sangaya Schools
advances.text: Boys leave home to board with a master of the Quran in the sangaya, the Kanuri school of the wooden slate. The schools spread letters through the empire and train the men who sit in Bornu's courts.

advances.name: Berber Camelry
advances.text: Berber camel riders serve as the empire's long-range desert force, capable of deep raids across the Sahara.

advances.name: Sharia Courts
advances.text: Islamic law courts replace customary justice, providing standardized legal procedures across Bornu's diverse territories.

advances.name: Ngazargamu Metropolis
advances.text: The fortified capital of Ngazargamu, enclosed by walls over six kilometers long, serves as the commercial and political heart of the empire.

advances.name: Tribute Economy
advances.text: Government revenue flows from tribute, customs duties, and participation in the slave trade that sustains the trans-Saharan caravan network.

advances.name: Mailed Cavalry Tradition
advances.text: Heavily armored horsemen in chainmail and iron helmets form the elite shock force of the Bornu army, charging in dense formations across the Sahelian grasslands.

advances.name: Cotton Industry
advances.text: Bornu's weavers produce fine cotton cloth that is traded across the Sahara, prized for its quality from Lake Chad to the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Bilma Salt Road
advances.text: Control of the Bilma oasis and its salt deposits gives Bornu a stranglehold on the central trans-Saharan route.

event.title: Masters of the Salt Road
event.text:
The great caravan route from Lake Chad to Tripoli passes through the salt oases of Bilma, where enormous deposits of natron and salt are extracted by the labor of thousands. Every caravan that crosses the Sahara must pass through Bornu's territory and pay our tolls. From Bilma through Fezzan to the Mediterranean, a river of wealth flows through our lands, natron, cotton, kola nuts, ivory, and ostrich feathers heading north, while horses, firearms, silk, and copper come south.

Our merchants have secured dominance over this central Saharan route, making Bornu the indispensable middleman between tropical Africa and the Mediterranean world.

options.text: Let the tolls flow into our treasury.

modifiers.name: Masters of the Bilma Road
modifiers.text: Our control over the Bilma oasis and the salt caravans that pass through it gives us unmatched leverage over trans-Saharan commerce.

advances.name: Diplomatic Network
advances.text: Bornu maintains diplomatic correspondence with the Ottoman Empire, the Hausa states, and North African kingdoms, projecting influence far beyond its borders.

advances.name: Scorched Earth Tactics
advances.text: Mai Alooma's soldiers burn everything in their path during campaigns, denying sustenance to enemies and breaking their will to resist.

advances.name: Fortified Cities
advances.text: Earthen ramparts encircle Bornu's great cities, that of Ngazargamu stretching over six kilometers in circumference. Within them the mai's quarter is raised in fired red brick.

advances.name: Standardized Measures
advances.text:
Standard units of measure for grain and trade goods, introduced under Alooma, facilitate commerce and tax collection across the empire. Cotton strips of a fixed width serve as money.

Available in: Cotton Weaving House

advances.name: Kotoko Flotilla
advances.text: The Kotoko boatmen of Lake Chad provide river transport, logistical support, and amphibious capability to the Bornu military.

advances.name: Kola Nut Trade
advances.text: Kola nuts from the southern forests are traded through Bornu's markets to destinations across the Sahara, prized as stimulants and ceremonial gifts.

advances.name: Legal Codification
advances.text: The codification of Islamic law under the Mais provides a uniform legal framework for governing Bornu's multi-ethnic territories.

advances.name: Imperial Cavalry
advances.text: The Bornu cavalry remains the backbone of the empire's military power, with generations of breeding producing the finest warhorses in the Sahel. The great fief holders ride to the muster with their followers in lebde, quilted armor that covers horse and man alike.

advances.name: Leather Workshops
advances.text: The vast herds around Lake Chad provide an abundance of hides, processed in Bornu's tanneries into leather goods exported across the trans-Saharan network.

advances.name: Scholarly Networks
advances.text: Bornu's ulama maintain connections to Islamic learning centers from Timbuktu to Cairo, ensuring the empire keeps pace with intellectual developments across the Muslim world.

advances.name: Sayfawa Twilight
advances.text: After seven centuries of rule, the world's longest-reigning dynasty faces mounting challenges from internal division and external threats.

event.title: The Twilight of the Sayfawa
event.text:
The Sayfawa dynasty, which has ruled for over seven centuries, the longest-reigning dynasty in recorded history, faces an existential crisis. Internal court intrigues have weakened the Mai's authority, provincial governors grow increasingly independent, and the old tribute-based economy falters as trade routes shift.

Yet the dynasty's name still carries immense weight. The Sayfawa trace their lineage to the legendary Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan, and their girgam, the royal chronicle, records an unbroken chain of sovereign Mais stretching back to the time of the Prophet. We must decide whether to shore up this ancient institution or embrace new forms of governance.

options.text: The Sayfawa are eternal. Restore the Mai's authority.

modifiers.name: Sayfawa Restoration
modifiers.text: The ancient dynasty reasserts its sacred authority, drawing upon centuries of legitimacy to bind the empire together through troubled times.

options.text: The Shehu shall rule where the Mai cannot.

modifiers.name: Embrace the Shehu
modifiers.text: The old dynasty gives way to practical governance. The Shehu's council rules through competence and military merit rather than bloodline.

advances.name: Reformed Musketeers
advances.text: A new generation of Bornu musketeers, better trained and equipped than their predecessors, takes the field in defense of the empire.

advances.name: Natron Monopoly
advances.text:
State control over natron extraction and export provides a steady revenue stream independent of the declining slave trade.

Available in: Natron Works

advances.name: Agricultural Reforms
advances.text: The resettlement of farmers to new lands and improvement of Lake Chad's irrigation systems expand the empire's agricultural base.

advances.name: Fortified Camps
advances.text:
Permanent military encampments with defensive walls project Bornu's power across its frontier territories.

Available in: Fortified War Camp

advances.name: Saharan Diplomacy
advances.text: Bornu's diplomatic reach extends across the Sahara, maintaining alliances and commercial relationships from Tripoli to the forest kingdoms.

advances.name: al-Kanemi Defense
advances.text: Muhammad al-Kanemi's defense of Bornu against the Fulani jihad preserved the empire when all seemed lost, establishing a new dynasty of warrior-scholars. He won it with the Kanembu spearmen who followed him out of Kanem.

event.title: The Defense of Bornu
event.text:
When the Fulani jihad erupted across Hausaland and the warriors of Usman dan Fodio swept eastward, it seemed that Bornu itself would fall. Ngazargamu, our ancient capital, was sacked in 1808. But Muhammad al-Kanemi, an Islamic scholar and military commander, rallied the Kanembu and Shuwa Arabs to the empire's defense. Leading a mixed force of students, mallams, and mercenaries, al-Kanemi defeated the jihadi forces and drove them from Bornu.

Al-Kanemi established a new capital at Kukawa and formed the Majlis, an executive council that brought together the empire's diverse communities. Though the Sayfawa Mais continued as figureheads, real power now rested with the Shehu and his council. Bornu survived where other Sahelian states did not.

advances.name: Kukawa Metropolis
advances.text: The new capital of Kukawa grows into one of sub-Saharan Africa's greatest cities, a center of commerce, scholarship, and governance, laid out along its dendal.

advances.name: Shehu Administration
advances.text: The al-Kanemi Shehus rule through the Majlis council, bringing efficient administration and collective governance to replace the old Mai system.

advances.name: Bornu Chronicles
advances.text: The tradition of the Diwan, Bornu's royal chronicle, and the girgam oral tradition preserve a millennium of history, fostering literacy and cultural identity.

advances.name: Trade Modernization
advances.text: New commercial infrastructure modernizes Bornu's trade networks, adapting centuries-old caravan routes to changing economic conditions.

advances.name: Majlis Governance
advances.text: The Majlis executive council, established by al-Kanemi, institutionalizes collective leadership and meritocratic governance in Bornu.

destiny.name: The Restoration of Kanem-Bornu
destiny.text: The ancient realm of the Sayfawa is reunited. Maintain stability and chart the empire's future course, whether as a military hegemon or a commercial crossroads.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Path of Kanem-Bornu
event.text: The reunification is complete. The Mai sits enthroned at Ngazargamu, the girgam records another chapter in the world's longest dynasty, and the empire stretches from the Sahara to the savanna. Now the real work begins, transforming this restored realm into something that will endure for centuries more.

destiny.name: The Hausa Campaigns
destiny.text: The wealthy Hausa city-states of Kano, Zaria and Katsina lie on our borders, their markets fat with goods and their walls ripe for siege. They are conquered and their wealth is brought under Bornu's lance.

event.title: The Fall of the Hausa Cities
event.text: Kano's walls have been breached and Zaria's emirs kneel before the Mai. The great Hausa city-states, long rivals of Bornu, now submit to our authority. Their dye pits, their forges, their teeming markets, all feed the treasury of Kanem-Bornu. The Sahel trembles.

options.text: The Hausa submit to Bornu's might.

destiny.name: Hegemony of the Sahel
destiny.text: Timbuktu, Gao and Djenne, the legendary cities of the western Sahel, are made to acknowledge Bornu's supremacy, and two thousand ducats are laid by. Dominion is claimed over the entire savanna belt.

conditions.text: Own Timbuktu, or a subject owns it
Own Gao, or a subject owns it
Own Djenné, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: Hegemon of the Sahel
event.text: From Timbuktu to Lake Chad, the entire Sahel belt acknowledges Bornu's supremacy. The great trading cities of the Niger bend now pay tribute, and our cavalry patrols the caravan routes unchallenged. But how shall we sustain this vast empire? Shall we extract wealth through raiding and tribute, or garrison our conquests with permanent forces?

options.text: Raid and tribute. Let the weak sustain us.

modifiers.name: Raider Economy
modifiers.text: The spoils of war flow into Bornu's treasury as raiding parties strip conquered territories of their wealth, sustaining the empire's military machine.

options.text: Garrison and fortify, hold what we have won.

modifiers.name: Garrison Network
modifiers.text: A network of permanent garrisons across the Sahel secures Bornu's conquests, with mercenary companies supplementing the imperial cavalry.

destiny.name: From Chad to the Sea
destiny.text: The trans-Saharan route ends on the Mediterranean at Tripoli and Misrata. Ghadames and both ports are taken, so that the entire caravan highway from Lake Chad to the sea is held.

conditions.text: Own Tripoli, or a subject owns it
Own Ghadames, or a subject owns it
Own Misratah, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Gold at least 3000

event.title: From Lake Chad to the Mediterranean
event.text: The impossible has been achieved. Bornu's armies have crossed the Sahara itself, seizing the Fezzan oases and the port of Tripoli. For the first time, a single power controls the entire trans-Saharan highway from the shores of Lake Chad to the Mediterranean Sea. The Mai of Kanem-Bornu now rules an empire that spans the desert.

options.text: We are the empire that bridges two worlds.

modifiers.name: Saharan Empire
modifiers.text: An empire spanning the desert, Bornu commands respect from the Mediterranean to the savanna, its nobles leading vast levies across every frontier.

options.text: Let our enemies know the terror of Bornu.

modifiers.name: Terror of the Sahel
modifiers.text: Bornu's reputation as an implacable military power reduces the will of enemies to resist, as reinforcements and levies arrive with terrifying speed.

destiny.name: Masters of the Salt Trade
destiny.text: Bilma's salt and natron flow through our markets to the wider world. Work natron in three of our places and secure our monopoly over the salt trade arteries of the central Sahara.

event.title: Lords of the Salt Road
event.text: The salt caravans of Bilma are the lifeblood of trans-Saharan trade, and now they flow entirely through our markets. With natron worked in our own pits beside the salt of Bilma, we have transformed Bornu from a mere waystation into the financial center of the central Sahara.

options.text: The salt flows through our hands.

destiny.name: Continental Crossroads
destiny.text: Ivory, cotton, kola nuts, and natron, Bornu sits at the center of Africa's greatest trade network. Bring ivory to our markets and build up Ngazargamu to 14 development, so that the capital becomes a true continental crossroads.

event.title: The Continental Crossroads
event.text: Ivory from the south, natron from Lake Chad, cotton from our looms, kola nuts from the forest kingdoms, every major commodity of interior Africa passes through Bornu's markets. We have become the indispensable hub of continental commerce, the crossroads where Africa's great trade routes converge. Shall we empower our merchant class to drive this growth, or shall the state collect its dues directly?

options.text: Empower the merchants. Let trade flourish.

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes of Bornu
modifiers.text: A rising class of wealthy Bornu merchants drives the integration of conquered peoples through shared commerce, their prosperity benefiting all estates.

options.text: The state shall collect its tolls.

modifiers.name: Toll Collectors of the Sahara
modifiers.text: State-appointed toll collectors at every oasis and market crossing ensure that Bornu extracts its share from every caravan and trader.

destiny.name: Master of the Trans-Saharan Network
destiny.text: Every caravan crossing the Sahara passes through our markets. With cotton in our markets and the salt oasis of Bilma built up to 10 development, Bornu commands the commerce of an entire continent.

event.title: Master of the Trans-Saharan Network
event.text: No caravan crosses the Sahara without passing through our markets. No trader reaches the Mediterranean without our consent. Bornu has achieved what no other Sahelian state could, total commercial dominance over the trans-Saharan network. The wealth of two continents flows through Lake Chad. How shall we use this power?

options.text: Build an emporium on the shores of Chad.

modifiers.name: Lake Chad Emporium
modifiers.text: The shores of Lake Chad host one of Africa's greatest emporiums, where goods from across the continent change hands and free trade flourishes under Bornu's protection.

options.text: Let our caravans carry diplomacy with trade.

modifiers.name: Caravan Diplomacy
modifiers.text: Bornu's caravans carry not only goods but diplomatic missions, spreading goodwill and innovation along the trade routes that bind the continent together.

units.name: Kanembu Cavalry
units.text: Armored horsemen of the Kanembu people, the traditional mounted elite of the Kanem-Bornu Empire, fighting in chainmail and iron helmets.

units.name: Iron Musketeers
units.text: Bornu's musketeers, trained by Ottoman military advisors, wear distinctive iron helmets and wield Turkish firearms with deadly precision.

units.name: Berber Camelry
units.text: Desert-hardened camel riders of Berber origin who serve as the empire's long-range raiding and reconnaissance force across the Sahara.

units.name: Mailed Cavalry
units.text: The elite of Bornu's cavalry, clad in full chainmail with iron helmets, mounted on armored horses bred for the charge.

units.name: Lebde Horse
units.text: Horsemen whose mounts and bodies are wrapped in lebde, thick quilted cotton stuffed with kapok. Arrows stick in it without reaching the man. It is also so heavy and so hot that these riders advance slowly and tire fast.

units.name: Kotoko Boatmen
units.text: Skilled rivermen of the Kotoko people who navigate Lake Chad and its tributaries, providing amphibious logistics and river transport.

units.name: Bornu Musketeers
units.text: The reformed musketeers of Bornu, disciplined and well-drilled, representing the modernized core of the empire's infantry.

units.name: Kanembu Spearmen
units.text: The Shehu's favorite troops: spearmen of the Kanembu who fight on foot in a close rank, behind tall shields cut from the light fogo wood that grows in the shallows of Lake Chad. They hold where horsemen scatter, but they bring spears to a field of muskets.

buildings.name: Natron Works
buildings.text: Extraction facilities for the valuable natron deposits found around Lake Chad, producing a key commodity for trans-Saharan trade.

where.text: Salt is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Ribat
buildings.text: A fortified frontier post combining military garrison with Islamic learning, guarding the empire's borders while spreading the faith.

buildings.name: Caravan Depot
buildings.text: A waystation and market for the trans-Saharan caravans, providing provisions, water, and trading facilities for merchants crossing the desert.

buildings.name: Sangaya
buildings.text: The Quran school of the Kanuri. Pupils come from far villages to board with a goni, a master who knows the whole Book by heart. They write each lesson on a wooden slate, wash it off when it is learned, and live on the alms of the town. Where a madrasa gathers scholars for the higher sciences, the sangaya teaches the Book itself to the sons of farmers and herdsmen.

buildings.name: Cotton Weaving House
buildings.text: A workshop where skilled weavers produce the fine cotton cloth for which Bornu is renowned across the trans-Saharan trade network.

buildings.name: Royal Brick Enclosure
buildings.text: Inside the earthen rampart of the city the mai's own quarter is walled in fired red brick, as at Birni Gazargamo and at Gambaru. The court, the Friday mosque and the armoury stand within it, and the city is ruled from behind its gates.

buildings.name: Bornu Tannery
buildings.text: A workshop for processing the abundant hides from Lake Chad's pastoral herds into leather goods for export.

buildings.name: Fortified War Camp
buildings.text: A permanent military encampment surrounded by defensive walls, projecting Bornu's military power across its frontier territories.

buildings.name: Lake Chad Fish Camp
buildings.text: A camp of fishermen on a shore rich in fish, where the catch is smoked and dried for the caravans.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Dendal
buildings.text: The broad avenue of a Kanuri capital, running from the gate to the ruler's palace. The court rides along it and the market spreads beside it. It is found only in the capital.

buildings.name: Imperial Barracks
buildings.text: A grand military complex where Bornu's elite soldiers train in firearms, cavalry tactics, and siege warfare, maintaining the empire's military edge.

buildings.name: Grand Caravansary
buildings.text: A vast commercial complex serving the trans-Saharan caravans, with warehouses, stables, lodgings, and market halls all enclosed within fortified walls.

list.name: Council of the Twelve
list.text: The institutional core of Sayfawa governance. The Mai ruled through twelve great offices, the Galadima as commander of the western marches and chancellor, the Yerima as warden of the salt routes and northern governor, the Kaigamarama as commander of the royal slave corps, the Mestrema as treasurer and master of horse, the Cirima as guardian of the youngest princes, and the lesser offices governing the wards of Birni Gazargamo. Each office carried a fief and a seat at the council; the Mai's word required the council's assent to be binding in custom.

list.name: Magira's Court
list.text: The institutionalised office of the queen-mother, held since the early Kanem period as a constitutional check on the Mai. The Magira commanded her own treasury, retinue, and palace at Birni Gazargamo, and her formal consent was required for the enthronement of a new Mai. The most famous holder, Aisa Kili Ngirmaramma, governed Bornu in her own name as regent c. 1564-70 during the minority of Idris Alooma and brokered the Ottoman embassy that brought Turkish musket-trainers to the kingdom. The institution was Sayfawa-specific and unparalleled in the wider Sahel.

list.name: Mamlukan Musketeers
list.text: The slave-soldier infantry corps founded by Mai Idris Alooma after his diplomatic mission of 1574 to the Ottoman governor of Tripoli, Mustafa Pasha. Turkish drillmasters instructed Bornu's slave-soldiers in the use of the matchlock; the corps was housed at the royal court, drew its salt and provisions from the Mai's stores, and answered to the Kaigamarama rather than to any provincial lord. The corps broke the Bulala at Garni Kiyala in 1577 and remained the spine of Bornu's standing forces until the Fulani jihad of 1808.

conditions.text: Has advance Gunpowder

list.name: Sayfawa Girgam
list.text: The Arabic-language chancery and royal chronicle of the Sayfawa Mais, maintained without break from the eleventh century to the fall of the dynasty. The Girgam recorded each Mai's accession, campaigns, marriages, and grants; it was supplemented by the Diwan salatin Bornu and by the Kitab ghazawat Idris of Ahmad ibn Furtu, the Mai's imam-chronicler. The chancery employed scribes drawn from the ulama and the Wangara diaspora; their writs gave juridical force to royal grants and bound succeeding generations to their fathers' obligations.

conditions.text: Sunnism religion

list.name: Kambasokis Compact
list.text: The working tribute-and-grazing arrangement by which the Sayfawa Mais bound the pastoral peoples of the basin, the Kanembu, the Toubou, the Buduma fishermen of the Lake Chad islands, and the Tuareg of the northern marches, to the throne. Each people rendered an annual tribute of cattle, salt-bars, slaves, or horses and a seasonal levy of cavalry; in exchange the Mai's troops kept the wells open, the raiders out, and the grazing rotations enforced. The compact ran in customary law rather than written code and fell heaviest on the sedentary cultivators along the Komadugu Yobe.
